This vignette starts from the outputs of the bonFIRE consensus peak calling pipeline, in
`<output_dir>/<prefix>/`:

- `<prefix>_final_tbl_w_metadata.tsv.gz`: one row per consensus peak per run (see the README for the columns)
- `<prefix>_transferred_cons_peaks_native_sequences_from_main_output.bed.gz`: the sequence of each consensus peak on each assembly

Every cutoff below is a parameter. Change them in the header above, or when rendering:

```r
rmarkdown::render("consensus_peak_vignette.Rmd",
                  params = list(input_dir = "/path/to/output_dir/my_sample/", prefix = "my_sample",
                                min_cov = 15, significance = "p", significance_cutoff = 0.01))
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(data.table)
library(Biostrings)
library(ggplot2)

tbl = fread(paste0(params$input_dir, params$prefix, "_final_tbl_w_metadata.tsv.gz"), na.strings = "NA")
dim(tbl)
```

# 1. Calling peaks

A consensus peak is a peak in a run if it passes all three cutoffs in that run:

| parameter | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `min_cov` | `r params$min_cov` | minimum coverage |
| `min_fire_cov` | `r params$min_fire_cov` | minimum FIRE coverage |
| `min_frac_acc` | `r params$min_frac_acc` | minimum fraction accessible (`fire_cov_OV_cov`) |

```{r call-peaks}
## peaks that weren't transferred to a run's assembly have NA coverage; %in% TRUE makes them FALSE
tbl[, is_peak := (coverage >= params$min_cov &
                  fire_coverage >= params$min_fire_cov &
                  fire_cov_OV_cov >= params$min_frac_acc) %in% TRUE]

## peaks called in each run
tbl[, .(consensus_peaks = .N, called_peaks = sum(is_peak)), by = sample_id]
```

# 2. Pairing the two haplotypes of each run

`sample_id` is the run followed by the assembly, e.g. `SMHT004_liver_SMHT004_1`. The last field
is the haplotype, and everything before it identifies the run.

If there are several runs per assembly (e.g. several tissues per donor), the run name may hold a
descriptor to group them by. Here that is a `tissue`, and the FDR correction below is done within
each one. With one run per assembly there is nothing to group by: leave `use_tissue` off
(`r params$use_tissue`) and every run is corrected together. `return_tissue` is an example of
pulling a descriptor out of the name; change it to match how your runs are named.

```{r haplotypes}
tbl[, haplotype := sub("^.*_", "", sample_id)]
tbl[, sample := sub("_[^_]*$", "", sample_id)]

## example: SMHT004_liver_SMHT004 -> liver; with a PS id, everything between it and the last
## field (HG00438_PS00991_ONT_HG00438 -> ONT)
return_tissue = function(sample){
  temp = strsplit(sample, "_")[[1]]
  if(grepl("_PS", sample)){
    return(paste0(temp[3:(length(temp)-1)], collapse = "_"))
  } else {
    return(temp[2])
  }
}
if(params$use_tissue){
  samples = unique(tbl$sample)
  tbl[, tissue := sapply(samples, return_tissue)[match(sample, samples)]]
} else {
  tbl[, tissue := "all"]
}

## haplotypes differ in copy number on chrX and chrY, so these can be left out of the test
tbl[, autosomal := !(cons_chr %in% c("chrY", "chrX")) & !(hg38_chr %in% c("chrY", "chrX"))]

unique(tbl[, .(sample, tissue)])
```

# 3. Does the underlying sequence match between haplotypes?

Sequences are in their own file (it has no header), one row per consensus peak on each assembly.
They are joined to the table by the peak's coordinates on that assembly.

```{r sequences}
seqs = fread(paste0(params$input_dir, params$prefix, "_transferred_cons_peaks_native_sequences_from_main_output.bed.gz"),
             header = FALSE, col.names = c("asm_chr", "asm_start", "asm_end", "consensus_peak_id", "seq"))
tbl = merge(tbl, unique(seqs), by = c("asm_chr", "asm_start", "asm_end", "consensus_peak_id"),
            all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)

## one row per consensus peak and run, with the two haplotypes side by side (coverage_1, coverage_2, ...)
tbl_haplotype = dcast(tbl, consensus_peak_id + sample + tissue + autosomal ~ haplotype,
                      value.var = c("coverage", "fire_coverage", "fire_cov_OV_cov", "is_peak", "seq"))
```

An assembly contig can run in either direction relative to the other haplotype's, so the two
sequences match if they are identical **or** one is the reverse complement of the other. They are
compared in upper case, in case an assembly is soft-masked.

```{r seqs-match}
tbl_haplotype[, seq_1 := toupper(seq_1)]
tbl_haplotype[, seq_2 := toupper(seq_2)]
has_seq_2 = which(!is.na(tbl_haplotype$seq_2))
seq_2_rev_comp = rep(NA_character_, nrow(tbl_haplotype))
seq_2_rev_comp[has_seq_2] = as.character(reverseComplement(DNAStringSet(tbl_haplotype$seq_2[has_seq_2])))
## NA if the peak is missing from either haplotype
tbl_haplotype[, seqs_match := fifelse(is.na(seq_1) | is.na(seq_2), NA,
                                      seq_1 == seq_2 | seq_1 == seq_2_rev_comp)]

tbl_haplotype[, .N, by = seqs_match]
```

# 4. Haplotype-selective peaks

For each run and consensus peak measured on both haplotypes, a Fisher's exact test compares FIRE
and non-FIRE coverage between them. P values are corrected (Benjamini–Hochberg) across all runs,
or within each tissue if `use_tissue` is on. A peak is called haplotype-selective if both haplotypes have at least `min_cov_hap_test`
(`r params$min_cov_hap_test`) coverage and its `significance` value is below
`significance_cutoff`. `significance` is `"fdr"` (the corrected p value, `fisher_fdr`) or `"p"`
(the raw p value, `fisher_p`); here it is the `r params$significance` below
`r params$significance_cutoff`. Both columns are kept, so you can also subset on either afterwards.

```{r hap-test}
tbl_haplotype_filt = tbl_haplotype[!is.na(coverage_1) & !is.na(coverage_2)]
if(params$exclude_sex_chrs){
  tbl_haplotype_filt = tbl_haplotype_filt[autosomal == TRUE]
}

tbl_haplotype_filt[, nonfire_1 := coverage_1 - fire_coverage_1]
tbl_haplotype_filt[, nonfire_2 := coverage_2 - fire_coverage_2]

## for very large tables, future.apply::future_mapply(..., future.seed = TRUE) runs this in parallel
tbl_haplotype_filt[, fisher_p := mapply(
  function(a, b, c, d) fisher.test(matrix(c(a, b, c, d), nrow = 2))$p.value,
  fire_coverage_1, nonfire_1, fire_coverage_2, nonfire_2
)]
tbl_haplotype_filt[, fisher_fdr := p.adjust(fisher_p, method = "BH"), by = tissue]

tbl_haplotype_filt[, both_haps_meet_min_coverage := coverage_1 >= params$min_cov_hap_test &
                                                     coverage_2 >= params$min_cov_hap_test]
stopifnot(params$significance %in% c("fdr", "p"))
significance_value = if(params$significance == "fdr") tbl_haplotype_filt$fisher_fdr else tbl_haplotype_filt$fisher_p
tbl_haplotype_filt[, hap_selective := significance_value < params$significance_cutoff & both_haps_meet_min_coverage]
tbl_haplotype_filt[, more_accessible_hap := fifelse(fire_cov_OV_cov_1 > fire_cov_OV_cov_2, "1", "2")]

tbl_haplotype_filt[, .(tested = .N, hap_selective = sum(hap_selective)), by = tissue]
```

A haplotype-selective peak whose sequences differ between the haplotypes may be driven by the
sequence change itself:

```{r hap-vs-seq}
tbl_haplotype_filt[, .N, by = .(hap_selective, seqs_match)][order(-hap_selective, seqs_match)]
```

```{r hap-plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5}
ggplot(tbl_haplotype_filt[both_haps_meet_min_coverage == TRUE],
       aes(x = fire_cov_OV_cov_1, y = fire_cov_OV_cov_2, colour = hap_selective)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey70", `TRUE` = "purple")) +
  labs(x = "fraction accessible, haplotype 1", y = "fraction accessible, haplotype 2",
       colour = "haplotype-selective") +
  theme_bw()
```

To save the results:

```{r save, eval = FALSE}
fwrite(tbl_haplotype_filt[, !c("seq_1", "seq_2")], paste0(params$prefix, "_hap_selective_peaks.tsv"),
       sep = "\t", na = "NA")
```
